chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: End of the big-band years, small groups and the Mahogany Hall band in Boston
summary: After Basie and Carter he worked in small groups with Newton, Bechet, Heywood, McPartland, Hackett and Max Kaminsky, and directed a band at Mahogany Hall in Boston.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When we were sort of talking about your associations before, your career, we got to Basie and then back to Benny Carter. And I guess that was about the end of your big band days.

Well, yes. Yes, it was, because then I started getting with the smaller groups, like Frankie Newton, and Sidney Bechet, Eddie Heywood, and Jimmy McPartland...and Bobby Hackett... I did some things with Max
Kaminsky. And, you know, I used to work down at Condon's, (Savoy) you know... And then I went to a room in Boston ...(?).... It wasn't my band. I just did...you know, directed it.
Were you at the Savoy in Boston?
No, I played at the Savoy with Edmond Hall. Then I had this band I was directing... This band I was directing was down at the...it was called Mahogany Hall in Boston.
Oh, yeah. That was George Wein's place.
Yeah. So I was kind of, like, in charge in the band,, but it wasn't really my band, you know.
Was that the band with Claude Hopkins and Doc Cheatham..? Buzzy Drootin
Buzzy Frankie(?). And his brother, Al?
He was a character! He had a face painted on his bass. He knew a lot of Ellington tunes.
Yeah. He wasn't a bad bass player. He was a strong cat on the bass, you know. Let's see, who else was there...?
Oh, there are so many when you get to remembering.
